title: PRD: Four-way Hosted Surface (Chat / Completions / Embeddings / Rerank) — Launch Readiness Playbook
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Summary:
This PRD defines the product, acceptance criteria, and launch playbook for a unified hosted API surface that simultaneously ships behavior-first contracts and operational controls for Chat, Completions, Embeddings, and Rerank. The goal is to provide a cohesive developer experience where a single onboarding flow and predictable SLAs unlock multi-feature use cases (e.g., retrieval-augmented generation with embeddings + rerank + chat) while keeping per-token economics transparent.

Problem statement:
Teams are currently integrating multiple discrete endpoints with inconsistent guarantees (latency, deterministic seeding, token accounting, streaming semantics). This causes higher friction for customers building combined flows and increases ops overhead for us. We need a single playbook that defines scope, compatibility, telemetry, rollout, and acceptance checks so we can ship a consistent multi-surface offering without regressing existing hosted customers.

Goals (outcomes):
- Developer ergonomics: single onboarding doc, unified SDK types, and deterministic behavior knobs documented.
- Operational confidence: launch with canary, eval-gated metrics, and rollback thresholds tied to quality regressions and latency SLOs.
- Cost transparency: per-route token-cost reporting in Console and clear guidance on batching/quantization.
- Interop: clients can compose Chat+Embeddings+Rerank with predictable semantics for streaming and structured output.

Scope (in):
- API surface contracts for Chat, Completions, Embeddings, Rerank (canonical request/response shapes).
- Streaming semantics alignment for Chat and Completions (partial tokens + event markers).
- Determinism seed behavior and guidance for seedempotent requests.
- Telemetry events: per-token latency, model_variant used, kv_cache_hit, batch_size, and quality_signals (eval test pass/fail).
- Canary rollout plan and evaluation harness (synthetic + customer beta).

Scope (out):
- Dedicated/DedicatedPrivate onboarding flows (separate workstreams).
- New model onboarding beyond the curated catalog (post-launch).

Personas:
- Integrator (software engineer): needs stable API and error behavior to build product flows.
- Platform Engineer (customer): needs cost and SLA signals in Console.
- Product Owner (Redwood): monitors quality regressions and rollout metrics.

Success metrics (quantitative):
- Post-launch quality: no more than 2 critical quality regressions during canary (regression defined as >5% drop in eval pass-rate for smoke prompt set).
- Latency SLOs: p95 token latency <= 90ms for online lane; p99 <= 250ms for generation under normal load.
- Adoption: 20 public integrations using combined surface within 90 days.
- Telemetry coverage: 95% of requests include model_variant and route tags in logs.

API contract highlights (developer-facing):
- Chat: streaming and non-streaming modes; initial message semantics include conversation_id and optional deterministic_seed; function/tool-calling preserved.
- Completions: single-turn generation with prompt templates; streaming SSE events follow same partial token envelope as Chat and include deterministic_seed support.
- Embeddings: batch input allowed, hex-encoded vector output optional; per-input idempotency_id accepted.
- Rerank: accepts embeddings or raw text; returns ordered candidate ids with optional confidence score; must accept candidate metadata passthrough.

Operational & Observability requirements:
- Console: per-route cost breakdown, token attribution by model_variant, realtime canary dashboard widget.
- Tracing: propagate request_id and sample up to 10% full traces for postmortem.
- Alerts: latency p99 >250ms for 10m => paged to SRE; quality regression alert tied to eval harness (see dependencies).

Security and compliance:
- All routes must respect tenant data isolation; telemetry must not include raw prompt text for customers who opt out (opt-out flag).
- KMS/HSM integration for private key material (for canary test data).
- Security review required: see security_review_required flag.

Rollout plan (high level):
1) Internal integ tests + e2e smoke suite (2 days).
2) Canary: 1% production traffic for 48 hours with daily eval-gated checks (synthetic prompts + customer beta seeds).
3) Gradual ramp: 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 50% over 7 days if all gates pass.
4) Full launch after 14 days of stable metrics and documentation published.

Rollback criteria (automatic):
- Quality: eval-gated failure: >5% relative drop in eval pass-rate vs baseline for 2 consecutive evaluation windows (4 hours) => immediate rollback.
- Latency: sustained p99 >250ms for 30 minutes AND error rate spike >0.5% => rollback.

Compatibility & migration notes:
- Backwards compatibility: endpoints maintain previous schema fields; new fields introduced as optional.
- Deprecation policy: if a field must change behavior, announce 90 days prior with migration guide.

Cost/Performance trade-offs considered:
- Default to lower-variance models for chat fast-lane; allow opt-in higher-quality models at higher per-token cost.
- Batching and prefix-KV caching enabled by default for embeddings routes to reduce unit cost; customers may disable for strict latency requirements.

- API contract spec (draft): https://confluence.redwood.company/prd/four-way-surface-spec
- Eval harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/evals/fourway-smoke (PR #421)
- Canary dashboard prototype: https://dashboards.redwood.company/g/fourway-canary
- Related ticket (dependency): PM-583741 (eval-driven acceptance)
acceptance_criteria: All four endpoints pass the eval smoke suite with >=95% pass-rate on balanced prompt set for two consecutive windows (4 hours each)
Streaming parity: Chat and Completions SSE streams deliver partial tokens in matching envelope and deliver final 'done' event identical in both implementations
Console telemetry shows per-route cost breakdown and model_variant attribution for >=95% of sampled requests
Canary rollout completes 48-hour 1% window with no automatic rollback triggers and no P0 incidents
API backward-compatibility: existing customers' SDK calls continue to succeed without changes to mandatory fields
Security review signed off and opt-out telemetry flow tested with a customer beta
checklist: Write final API contract and publish to Confluence
Engineering: implement deterministic_seed for Chat and Completions
Engineering: add batch embeddings optimization and per-input idempotency
Console: add per-route cost widget and sample traces
QA: run cross-protocol smoke harness against staging and recorded traffic
SRE: configure canary routing and automated rollback hooks
Design: doc examples for combined flows (RAG example with embeddings + rerank + chat)
Docs/DevX: SDK examples and migration guide published
Security: KMS/HSM review completed and opt-out telemetry validated
Legal/Compliance: add retention guidance for customer prompt data
